evidence.bullet: EAL support is for pupils whose first language is not English and who need English proficiency
evidence.quote: This is specifically for pupils whose first language is not English and who need support in gaining English proficiency to fully access the mainstream curriculum

evidence.bullet: A new arrival assessment meeting follows once the pupil is registered at an Island school
evidence.quote: is needed for eligible pupils once they are registered at an Isle of Man school

evidence.bullet: The meeting clarifies the level of need and lets the EAL Service advise on a starting plan
evidence.quote: The meeting will clarify the level of need and support for the pupil and will enable the EAL Service to advise on a starting plan

evidence.bullet: The EAL Service works with schools and parents on the admission and progress of such pupils
evidence.quote: The EAL Service supports schools and parents in the admission and progress of pupils who must learn English as part of their transition to a new educational setting

evidence.bullet: Short-term reception support can sometimes be given where the family uses another language
evidence.quote: short-term support can sometimes be provided for children who need extra help to settle when their family uses a different first language at home

sources.label: English as an Additional Language, Department of Education, Sport and Culture, Isle of Man
